scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a "rollback" on r13, R11 reports it lost an EIGRP
neighbor and 113.1.x.x routes disappeared from R11's topology
table. R13 reports EIGRP is running and its config looks valid.
What changed?

injection.action: change EIGRP AS from 100 to 300 (a value R11 doesn't speak)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r13 EIGRP AS number
Mechanism: EIGRP requires both ends of an adjacency to share
  the same AS. R11 runs AS 100 (covering both R12 and R13
  sides per the collapsed-single-AS fix from earlier). R13
  was reconfigured to AS 300. Hello packets carry the AS,
  the mismatch is detected, and the adjacency never forms.
  R11 stops seeing 113.1.x routes, and R13 stops seeing
  102.x / 112.x / 120.x routes from R12 via R11.
Localization: r13
Root cause: EIGRP AS mismatch (R13 in AS 300, R11/R12 in AS 100)
Fix: re-configure r13 to AS 100
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: EIGRP AS number / EIGRP autonomous system

agent.diagnosis_text:
The root cause is an EIGRP Autonomous System number mismatch introduced on r13
by the "rollback" operation. R13's on-disk startup configuration (frr.conf)
correctly declares `router eigrp 100`, with an inline comment noting that the
AS was deliberately renumbered from Cisco's original 300 to 100 so it would
match R11 (FRR's eigrpd cannot maintain two EIGRP instances simultaneously).
The rollback overwrote the running configuration with a stale pre-translation
version that still contains `router eigrp 300`. R11 has never changed and
continues to run AS 100.

EIGRP will only form an adjacency between peers that share the same AS number.
Because R13 now advertises Hello packets carrying AS 300 while R11 listens only
for AS 100 hellos, R11's eigrpd silently discards every Hello arriving on its
eth2 interface (FF segment). No neighbour relationship is established, so R13's
113.1.1.0/24 through 113.1.4.0/24 prefixes are never sent to R11, causing them
to vanish from R11's EIGRP topology and routing tables. R13's own topology table
is empty — it has zero neighbours in its newly instantiated AS 300 process,
confirming no peer has matched it.

The link layer is entirely healthy (r11.eth2 ↔ r13.eth0 both UP, 103.1.1.1/8
↔ 103.1.1.2/8). The fault is purely a control-plane misconfiguration confined
to r13.

Corrective fix: on r13, remove the incorrect process and restore the correct
one:
  `no router eigrp 300`
  `router eigrp 100` with the same network statements (103.0.0.0/8,
  113.1.1.0/24 – 113.1.4.0/24).
Alternatively, reload frr from the existing (correct) frr.conf on disk. The
neighbour adjacency and 113.1.x.x routes will re-appear on R11 within seconds.

Recommends removing the wrong EIGRP process and configuring r13 with AS 100 (or reloading the correct frr.conf), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by the collected evidence: running configs (R11=EIGRP 100, R13=EIGRP 300), on-disk frr.conf (R13 shows EIGRP 100), neighbor tables (R11 has neighbors only on AS100 side; R13 shows no neighbors under AS300), and interface IPs/up.
